stem.en: Two tubes of muddy water are spun in a centrifuge. Tube P runs at full speed and tube Q at half speed, and each runs until nothing more changes. How do the results compare?

text.en: P has a mud layer at the bottom, and Q stays cloudy, because a slow spin gives no push.
Both have the same two layers, and Q took longer to get there.
Both have the mud in the middle of the tube, and P has more of it.
P has much cleaner water than Q, because more speed always separates more.

explanation.en: Speed changes the time, not the end result. Half the speed gives a quarter of the push, so Q takes about four times as long, but it ends with the same mud at the bottom and clearer water on top. The tempting idea is that a faster spin separates more. A slow spin still pushes the mud outwards, only more gently.

hints.en: A slower spin still pushes the mud outwards. What does the lower speed change?
Does the speed decide how much separates, or how long it takes?
